newsitem.title: FRANCE: Britain still has long way to go on Europe - France.
newsitem.headline: Britain still has long way to go on Europe - France.

text.p: Tony Blair's landslide victory in last week's British general election was a defeat for anti-European sentiment but London still has a long way to go to get to the heart of Europe, French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Monday.

"It seems to me that there is movement towards Europe in Great Britain, but there is a truly great gap between the British position and what I would call the position of a reasonable Europe," he said in an interview on France 2 television.
The new British cabinet "has a long road ahead of it" in this regard, he added.

Three weeks ahead of the first round of a French parliamentary election, both the right and the left in France have attempted to claim Blair as one of their own, and the centre-rightist de Charette was no exception.
While acknowledging that the Labour Party leader was on the left, he drew a line between Blair's "modern left" and the French left, which was, he insisted, "different".
